# Disagreement Log — Gospel of Thomas, Saying 4

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Saying:** GTH 004
**Total Disagreements:** 4

---

## Disagreement 1 — "person old in days" vs. "old man"

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET/LOGOS:** "the person who is old in days"
**PNEUMA:** "an old man"
**Issue:** Coptic *ouroome šobs* is literally "a person old." The Semitic idiom "old in days" (cf. Dan 7:9 "Ancient of Days") carries deliberate resonance. "Old man" is natural English but loses the idiom.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Old in days" retained.

---

## Disagreement 2 — "child of seven days" vs. "week-old infant"

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET/LOGOS:** "child of seven days"
**PNEUMA:** "week-old infant"
**Issue:** "Seven days" has symbolic force (pre-circumcision, the eighth day as circumcision day in Jewish practice); "week-old infant" loses this resonance.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Child of seven days" retained.

---

## Disagreement 3 — "place of life" vs. "where life is found"

**Verse:** v.1
**EMET/LOGOS:** "place of life"
**PNEUMA:** "where life is found"
**Issue:** PNEUMA converts the nominal phrase into a question-form that imports an interrogative not in the Coptic.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Place of life" retained.

---

## Disagreement 4 — "a single one" vs. "one"

**Verse:** v.3
**EMET/LOGOS:** "a single one"
**PNEUMA:** "one"
**Issue:** *Ouah ouōt* is emphatic — "one alone," "a single one." The reduplication matters and recurs as a technical term throughout the collection.
**Resolution (SOPHIA):** "A single one" retained as technical term.

---
